task.instruction: Find a report on the BBC News website about recent developments in renewable energy technologies in the UK.

final_answer:
I found a BBC News report on a recent UK renewable energy development: **"Geothermal plant plans to drill four more wells"** (BBC News, Cornwall — 28 October 2026, by Lee Trewhela of the Local Democracy Reporting Service). Link: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crjwe84lqj10o

**What it reports:** Eden Geothermal, operator of the UK's first geothermal power plant at the Eden Project in Cornwall, wants to increase its permitted underground wells from two to six — drilling four additional wells to boost capacity "without the need to extend beyond the approved boundary or substantially alter what has already been approved." Other proposed changes include a larger air-cooled condenser bank, reconfigured site buildings, two substations instead of the one previously agreed with Cornwall Council, and a smaller water storage lagoon. The company says the amendments offer "a significant benefit in terms of increasing the renewable energy generated on site."

The existing well reaches about 5km (3.1 miles) below the surface and taps water at up to 200C (390F), heating Eden's greenhouses and rainforest biome; a second, similarly sized well was approved in December 2010 but has not yet been drilled. Nearby residents can discuss the plans at Trethurgy Village Hall on Wednesday 15:00–19:00 GMT and on 6 November 15:00–18:00, with a determination date of 18 November. Cornwall Council's landscape team supported the mitigation measures, though it noted construction "may involve disturbance" from dust and noise.

If you'd prefer a different angle, the same search surfaced other recent UK renewables stories — for example "Construction begins on Lewis Hub electricity project" (a subsea cable to carry Western Isles power to the mainland) and "Dales wind farm would 'spoil' view, says former PM."

judge.rationale: The agent found and summarized a BBC News article dated 28 Oct 2026 about UK geothermal renewable energy developments in Cornwall, with URL and page text evidence.
